entries.note: PMID 15829967 resolves; quote verbatim in abstract; print 2005-04-14. Untested correct: no patient PAR data in 2005. Model matches the BRCA-deficient cell panels the FDA review lists.

PMID 19553641; all quotes verbatim in abstract (NEJM full text Cloudflare-blocked). 'Confirmed PARP inhibition' in PBMC/hair/tumour supports same at the cf-cftr precedent level; comparison_stated=false is honest. Registry: start 2005-07-11, no results posted.

PMID 18971340; quote verbatim in abstract; epub 2008-10-29, print 2008-11-04. Untested correct. Caveat: this GEMM is not the model tested in 2014 (HBCx-10 PDX, initiated 2011-11-25), so opener and tested model differ.

Quote verbatim (pdf p.42); Figure 15 states the comparison; only 400 mg put every patient above IC90. FDA itself calls it an 'exploratory analysis' to 'justify the clinical dose'; PDX study began 2011-11-25, after dose selection. Same under the letter; rule question 1.
PMID 15829966; quote verbatim in full text (nature.com served full HTML); print 2005-04-14. Untested correct; model_filed plausible (BRCA-deficient xenografts appear in the FDA review).

Quotes verbatim (abstract). Abstract frames the trial as evaluation of the 'potential synthetic lethal therapeutic strategy' with carrier enrichment; Bryant/Farmer (2005-04-14) precede first dosing (2005-07-11): genuine prospective test. comparison_stated=true is a 'frames itself' reading, not side-by-side data; rule question 4.

PMID 15829966; quote verbatim in full text. Untested correct. But the filed safety model is rat/dog repeat-dose toxicology, which existed before first dosing (2005-07-11); the opener should name it (model_first_use_year <=2005).

Quote verbatim (abstract). Named model is not the filed safety model (rat/dog tox); its silence on marrow toxicity failed (grade 4 thrombocytopenia DLT), which ad-amyloid scores as contra. Propose untested on the tox model, or drop the entry; 2005 already opens the strip.

Quote verbatim (pdf p.16). Reviewer: hematopoietic target organ 'consistent with adverse reactions reported in patients' (match correct). Cytopenias at >=2%/4% of clinical AUC; animal maxima only 2-18%/12-26% of human AUC. Direction held: same stands under v2; magnitude recorded; rule question 2.

Dose quote on printed p.35 (pdf 42); safety quote on printed p.9 (pdf 16); HBCx-10 study = Pharmacology Report 27, initiated 2011-11-25; margins: rat/dog cytopenias at >=2%/4% of clinical AUC, animal maximum exposures 2-18% (rat) and 12-26% (dog) of human AUC (pdf 138).
fact_field_checks.judgement_claims: Murai 2012 abstract confirms niraparib > olaparib >> veliparib trapping; the '~10-fold less cytotoxic' figure is full-text and not checked. Hopkins 2019 'consistent with emerging clinical data' is verbatim in the abstract.
fact_field_checks.model_first_use_year_safety3: Draft has null. Not pinned exactly: rat/dog GLP toxicology necessarily preceded first-in-human dosing on 2005-07-11; the review's parseable study-initiation dates are 2007 (batch-comparison rat, reproductive studies). Suggest <=2005 with that inference stated.

missing: Ovarian-specific efficacy comparison: Fong 2010 J Clin Oncol, doi 10.1200/JCO.2009.26.9589 (PMID 20406929, print 2010-05-20): 50 BRCA-mutant ovarian patients, clinical benefit 46%, framed as the synthetic-lethal strategy; stronger for an ovarian context than the mixed-tumour phase 1. Candidate second `same` in efficacy (2010) or swap.

Iniparib is never mentioned. Worth one line in the efficacy judgement: its TNBC phase 3 failure (O'Shaughnessy 2014, doi 10.1200/JCO.2013.52.4942) is not a class failure because the cell model showed it neither inhibits PARP nor kills HR-deficient cells (Patel 2012, doi 10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-11-2890), and it was not ovarian. No status change.

Safety strip opener: rat/dog repeat-dose toxicology is the filed safety model and existed before 2005-07-11; the cell should open on it (untested, <=2005), making the 2014 entry the only `same` and resolving the drafter's own 'second consecutive same' concern.
rule_questions: Dose 2014: the IC90 'prediction' came from a PDX PK/PD study begun 2011-11-25, after phase 1 (2005-2008) and the 100-vs-400 mg phase 2 (2007-2009); the FDA calls it an 'exploratory analysis ... to justify the clinical dose'. Rules 1 and 5 admit it as a published comparison (same); the atlas's framing ('predictions compared with what happened') does not. If a prediction must precede the patient data, this is untested.

Safety 2014: direction correct (marrow target organ) but animals showed cytopenias at >=2%/4% of clinical AUC and never reached human exposure, i.e. a conservative exposure miss of 25-50x with no safety margin. v2 says magnitude does not change the status, so same stands; decide whether a magnitude or safety-margin threshold should gate same vs contra for safety cells.

Safety 2009: a model that was half-right (tumour selectivity held; marrow toxicity unmodelled, grade 4 thrombocytopenia DLT) while a different model (rat/dog tox) caught the toxicity. The '(or its silence)' clause plus the ad-amyloid precedent would score the silence as contra; the brief's best-model rule says the knockout/cell model is the wrong model for the question. Which applies?

comparison_stated semantics: a trial that designs itself as a test of a model-derived hypothesis but reports no model data (Fong 2009) is scored true in efficacy and false in engagement from the same source. Define whether 'frames itself as the test' counts as 'side by side'.
One entry per change of status vs model change within a cell (dose 1->2, safety 2->3): the brief forbids consecutive identical statuses but does not say what to do when the best model changes.
